description: Source-backed operational date overrides for GeoNames-derived military base overlay records. These overrides are deliberately conservative and use year-level precision unless the source evidence supports more. Includes manual official-source overrides plus reviewed exact GeoNames ID Wikidata P1566 backfill candidates.

operational_intervals.label: Las Vegas Army Airfield / wartime gunnery school phase
Las Vegas Air Force Base / Nellis Air Force Base phase

overrides.source_notes: Official Nellis history notes 1941 construction/origins, standby at the end of 1946, and reopening on 4 January 1949.

overrides.name: Alconbury Royal Air Force Base
overrides.source_notes: U.S. Air Force 501st Combat Support Wing history says RAF Alconbury opened in 1938 as a grass satellite airfield for RAF Upwood. Current end left open because the source describes continuing base use.

overrides.name: Coningsby Royal Air Force Base
overrides.source_notes: Official RAF Coningsby history lists 1941 as the year RAF Coningsby opened. Current end left open because the RAF station page lists active current units and aircraft.

overrides.name: Cosford Royal Air Force Base
overrides.source_notes: Official RAF Cosford history says No. 2 School of Technical Training was stood up and the station formally opened on 15 July 1938. Current end left open because current RAF pages continue to describe RAF Cosford activity.

overrides.name: Fairford Royal Air Force Base
overrides.source_notes: U.S. Air Force 501st Combat Support Wing article says Fairford was constructed in 1943-44. Candidate uses 1944 as the first full operational year and marks medium confidence to avoid over-precise interpretation of a construction range.

overrides.name: Faslane Base
overrides.source_notes: Royal Navy page identifies HMNB Clyde/Faslane as the current submarine-service base. GOV.UK CASD history says HMS Resolution completed the first deterrent patrol in June 1968 and all four Resolution-class submarines were ported and operated from HMNB Clyde. Candidate uses 1968 for the high-confidence nuclear-submarine operational phase, not an assertion that no naval activity existed earlier.

overrides.name: HMNB Portsmouth
overrides.source_notes: Royal Museums Greenwich says Portsmouth Dockyard was established in 1495 by Henry VII and remains one of the oldest dockyards still in operation. Science Museum Group collection timeline also starts Portsmouth Dockyard in 1495. Current end left open for active HMNB Portsmouth.

overrides.name: Honington Royal Air Force Base
overrides.source_notes: Official RAF Honington history says RAF Honington opened in 1937 and the key dates list 1937 as the station founding year. Current end left open because the RAF describes the station as the home of the RAF Regiment and RAF Police.

overrides.name: RAF Benson
overrides.source_notes: Official RAF Benson history says the station opened on 1 February 1939 and accepted its first aircraft. Current end left open because the page describes active Joint Aviation Command and resident-unit outputs.

overrides.name: RAF Brize Norton
overrides.source_notes: Official RAF Brize Norton history says the station officially opened on 13 August 1937. Current end left open because the page lists current transport and air-mobility aircraft.

overrides.name: RAF Odiham
overrides.source_notes: Official RAF Odiham history says the station formally became RAF Odiham on 11 January 1937 and key dates list 1937 as official opening. Current end left open because the page describes it as the active home of the UK Chinook Force.

overrides.name: RAF Welford
overrides.source_notes: U.S. Air Force 501st Combat Support Wing memorial article says Memorial Grove was established in 1993, 50 years after Welford became a joint RAF-USAF base. Candidate derives 1943 from that dated statement and keeps confidence medium because this is an anniversary inference.

overrides.name: Royal Air Force Valley
overrides.source_notes: Official RAF Valley history says the station opened in February 1941 as RAF Rhosneigr. Current end left open because the page describes active flying training outputs.

overrides.name: Cazaux
overrides.source_notes: French Ministry of Armed Forces reserve/housing pages describe Base aerienne 120 Cazaux as implanted/created at Cazaux in 1913 for aerial-gunnery crew instruction. Current end left open because the same ministry pages describe active BA 120 functions.

overrides.name: Istres-Le Tube Air Base
overrides.source_notes: French Ministry of Armed Forces pages say the site hosted pilot training from 1917, became an operational base in 1940, hosted American forces in 1944, and the French Air Force reinstalled permanently in 1947; BA 125 is installed on the site from 1949. Candidate uses 1917 for first military aviation use and leaves end open for active BA 125.

overrides.name: Mont-de-Marsan
overrides.source_notes: French Ministry of Armed Forces 14 July presentation dossier identifies Base aerienne 118 Colonel Rozanoff as created in 1945 and located at Mont-de-Marsan. Current end left open for active BA 118.

overrides.name: Orange-Caritat
overrides.source_notes: French Ministry of Armed Forces BA 115 history says the base was inaugurated in 1939, occupied from 1942 to 1944, hosted the RAF until 1951, and has continued the south-east air-safety posture since the 5th wing returned. Current end left open because the ministry describes current Rafale infrastructure and units at Orange.

overrides.name: Orleans-Bricy Air Base
overrides.source_notes: French Ministry of Armed Forces infrastructure article says BA 123 Orleans-Bricy dates to 1938; another ministry article describes ongoing transformation and 90 years of military history. Current end left open for active BA 123.

overrides.name: Salon
overrides.source_notes: French Ministry of Armed Forces BA 701 page says the base has been implanted in Salon-de-Provence since 1937. Current end left open because the same page describes current BA 701, Ecole de l'air et de l'espace, and Patrouille de France activity.

overrides.name: Landivisiau
overrides.source_notes: French Ministry of Armed Forces / Marine nationale says the BAN Landivisiau was created/inaugurated in 1965 and became operational in 1967 with embarked fighter flotillas. Candidate uses 1965 for base creation and leaves end open for active naval aviation use.

overrides.name: Evreux-Fauville Air Base

operational_intervals.label: USAF Evreux Air Base construction and American era
French Base aerienne 105 phase

overrides.source_notes: French Ministry of Armed Forces material says Evreux Air Base was constructed from 1952 to 1954 for the American era and BA 105 was created in 1967 after return to France. Candidate uses intervals to preserve that operator transition.

overrides.name: Ramstein
overrides.source_notes: Official Ramstein Air Base history identifies the anniversary of Ramstein Air Base as 5 August 1952 and says French forces began construction in 1951 before U.S. forces took over in 1952. Current end left open for active Ramstein Air Base.

overrides.name: Wiesbaden
overrides.source_notes: Official U.S. Army Garrison Wiesbaden history says Wiesbaden Airfield was designated as a fliegerhorst/air base in 1936, construction was completed in 1938, and the first German military unit occupied it. Current end left open because it remains Lucius D. Clay Kaserne / Wiesbaden Army Airfield.

overrides.name: RAF Geilenkirchen (historical)

operational_intervals.label: RAF Geilenkirchen fighter-squadron base
German missile unit and US Army artillery detachment phase
NATO Air Base Geilenkirchen / E-3A Component phase

overrides.source_notes: NATO newcomer guide says the RAF used Geilenkirchen from May 1953 until RAF flying operations ended in January 1968; Germany took over in March 1968; NATO conversion work began in 1980; and Germany formally handed the air base to NATO on 31 March 1982. Current NATO page confirms ongoing NATO Air Base Geilenkirchen use.

overrides.name: Nordholz Naval Airbase

operational_intervals.label: Imperial German naval airship and flight operations
Bundeswehr naval air station phase

overrides.source_notes: Marineflieger historical page says flight operations at Nordholz began in September 1914 and the Marinefliegerhorst Nordholz was commissioned for Bundeswehr naval aviation on 26 April 1963. Marked medium because the source is near-official/specialist rather than a bundeswehr.de page.

overrides.name: Norvenich Air Base
overrides.source_notes: German Armed Forces Association article says the Luftwaffe occupied Nörvenich as one of the first three Bundeswehr sites in early 1956. 24Rhein, citing Bundeswehr context, says the RAF Germany base was handed to the German defence ministry in December 1955. Candidate uses 1955 for handover/start of Bundeswehr phase and marks medium confidence because a direct Bundeswehr history page was not located in this pass.

overrides.name: Lechfeld Air Base
overrides.source_notes: Specialist encyclopedia mirror lists Fliegerhorst Lechfeld opening in 1912 and describes continued Bundeswehr operation. Marked medium and included as a candidate only; prefer replacing with a Bundeswehr or local-government source before committing to the production override file.

overrides.name: Lager Hammelburg
overrides.source_notes: City of Hammelburg brochure says Lager/Truppenubungsplatz Hammelburg has had a military tradition since 1895 and is used as a Bundeswehr training center. Marked medium because this is a municipal tourism/overview source, not a dedicated Bundeswehr installation history.

overrides.name: Chievres Air Base
overrides.source_notes: Official U.S. Army Garrison Benelux pages identify Chièvres Air Base as the current USAG Benelux headquarters / SHAPE-support NATO airfield and say the NATO/SHAPE Support Group moved to Belgium in 1967. Candidate uses 1967 for current NATO/US support phase, not for the earlier Belgian/German airfield history.

overrides.name: Beja Airbase
overrides.source_notes: Portuguese Air Force BA11 page says Base Aerea No. 11 at Beja was created in 1964 by Portaria No. 20856 of 21 October to support Portuguese-West German operational training agreements. Current end left open for active BA11.

overrides.name: Altus Air Force Base

operational_intervals.label: Altus Army Air Field wartime training phase
Postwar Air Force base phase

overrides.source_notes: Official Altus chronology says the War Department established Altus Army Air Field in 1942, flying training began in January 1943, the field was placed inactive/surplus in 1945, and SAC assumed control in 1953.

overrides.name: Keesler Air Force Base
overrides.source_notes: Official Keesler history says the War Department activated Army Air Corps Station No. 8 at Biloxi in June 1941 and officially designated it Keesler Army Airfield in August 1941.

overrides.name: Cape Canaveral Air Force Station
overrides.source_notes: Official Space Launch Delta 45 history places the Cape Canaveral military launch-range origin in the 1949 Joint Long Range Proving Ground period; first launch activity followed in 1950.

overrides.name: Dobbins Air Reserve Base
overrides.source_notes: Official Dobbins fact sheet says Dobbins ARB was built in 1943 as Marietta Army Airfield and was renamed Dobbins Air Reserve Base in 1992.

overrides.name: Dyess Air Force Base

operational_intervals.label: Abilene Army Air Base / Army Airfield phase
Abilene AFB / Dyess AFB phase

overrides.source_notes: Official Dyess history says Abilene Army Air Base opened in December 1942, was inactive by early 1946, and the 4021st Air Base Squadron activated at Abilene Air Force Base in January 1955 before the Dyess renaming in 1956.

overrides.name: Elmendorf Air Force Base
overrides.source_notes: Official JBER history lists Elmendorf's establishment in June 1940, construction beginning in June 1940, and first Air Corps personnel arriving in August 1940.

overrides.name: Fairchild Air Force Base
overrides.source_notes: Official Fairchild history says the base has been integral since 1942 and the depot activated at Spokane in March 1942.

overrides.name: Francis E Warren Air Force Base
overrides.source_notes: Official Warren history says Fort D. A. Russell was established in 1867 and identifies F. E. Warren as the oldest continuously active military installation in the Air Force.

overrides.name: Warren Air Force Base
overrides.source_notes: Duplicate GeoNames Warren record; same official Fort D. A. Russell/F. E. Warren continuity applies.

overrides.name: Goodfellow Air Force Base
overrides.source_notes: Official Goodfellow history says the airfield was established in 1940, ready for occupancy in January 1941, and first students arrived in February 1941; use 1941 for operational visibility.

overrides.name: Grand Forks Air Force Base
overrides.source_notes: Official Grand Forks environmental history material and near-official base-history summaries place construction in the mid-1950s and operational/occupied use in early 1957.

overrides.name: Hill Air Force Base
overrides.source_notes: Official Hill history says the first Ogden Air Depot commander arrived at Hill Field in November 1940, marking official operations at the field.

overrides.name: Homestead Air Force Base

operational_intervals.label: Homestead Army Air Field wartime phase
Homestead Air Force Base / Air Reserve Base phase

overrides.source_notes: Official Homestead history-office PDF references September 1942 activation/origin. The 1953 postwar reopening and continued reserve-base use are strong but should receive a second official confirmation before applying as high confidence.

overrides.name: Hurlburt Field
overrides.source_notes: Official Hurlburt pages identify the site as Eglin Auxiliary Field No. 9, one of the 1940s auxiliary training fields, and note the Hurlburt naming after a 1943 crash. Use 1943 as a conservative candidate pending a stronger exact operational opening source.

overrides.name: Joint Base Andrews
overrides.source_notes: Official Joint Base Andrews history says Camp Springs Army Air Field became operational in May 1943 and later became Andrews Field/Air Force Base.

overrides.name: Joint Base Langley-Eustis
overrides.source_notes: Official JBLE pages mark the Langley deed/founding in 1916; official AICUZ history describes Langley AFB as established in 1917. Use 1917 for operational facility visibility and avoid treating the 2010 joint-base name as the operational start.

overrides.name: Kelly Field Annex

operational_intervals.label: Kelly Field / Kelly Air Force Base phase
Kelly Field Annex / joint-use military airfield phase

overrides.source_notes: Official JBSA articles say Kelly Field was founded in 1917, Kelly AFB closed in July 2001, and the Kelly Field/Annex name and joint-use military airfield role continued afterward.

overrides.name: Laughlin Air Force Base

operational_intervals.label: Laughlin Army Air Field wartime phase
Reopened Laughlin Air Force Base phase

overrides.source_notes: Official Laughlin history says Laughlin Army Air Field began in July 1942, the Army decided to close it in September 1945, and the Air Force reopened Laughlin AFB in May 1952.

overrides.name: Luke Air Force Base

operational_intervals.label: Luke Field wartime fighter-training phase
Reactivated Luke Air Force Base phase

overrides.source_notes: Official Luke air-park history says the facility became Luke Field in June 1941, closed in November 1946, and was reactivated as Luke AFB in February 1951.

overrides.name: Marine Corps Air Station Beaufort
overrides.source_notes: Official Marine Corps environmental/history documents identify the site as Naval Air Station Beaufort commissioned in 1943 and later MCAS Beaufort.

overrides.name: McChord Field Airport (Joint Base Lewis-McChord)
overrides.source_notes: Official McChord article confirms the 1938 McChord Field naming; near-official HistoryLink history says the military takeover occurred in 1938 and the official McChord Field dedication occurred in July 1940. Use 1940 for operational military-field visibility.

overrides.name: McGuire Air Force Base

overrides.name: Daisan Kanku Kaijo Hoan Honbu Yokohama Kido Bojo Kichi
overrides.source_notes: Japanese National Personnel Authority/JCG award page says Yokohama Mobile Disaster Prevention Base was established in April 1998; JCG map confirms current base.

overrides.name: Kaijo Hoancho Sodegaura Bunshitsu
overrides.source_notes: Official Chiba Coast Guard history says Sodegaura branch was installed 1972-05-01 and integrated into Chiba Coast Guard Office on 2010-03-31.

overrides.name: Katsuura Kaijo Hoansho
overrides.source_notes: Official Choshi/JCG page lists Katsuura Coast Guard Station and says Katsuura branch was promoted to station in 1962.

overrides.name: Nagoyako Kaijo Kotsu Center
overrides.source_notes: JCG current page confirms Nagoya-ko VTS Center; 1994 Transport White Paper reports JCG opened the Nagoya Port Maritime Traffic Center on 1994-07-15.

overrides.name: Shonan Kaijo Hoansho
overrides.source_notes: MLIT white paper says Yokosuka Coast Guard Office Shonan Coast Guard Station began 2002-04-01; MLIT Kanto page confirms the current 2017-built Shonan facility.

overrides.name: Champ de manoeuvre Chilcotin
overrides.source_notes: French alias for Chilcotin Training Area. DND's 1923 report lists Chilcotin, B.C. Training Area land acquired from British Columbia; BC Geographical Names ties Champ de manoeuvre Chilcotin/Canadian Forces Camp Chilcotin to the official Chilcotin Training Area; CanadaBuys/DND material says the area is DND-owned and used as a military training area.

overrides.name: Chilcotin Training Area
overrides.source_notes: DND's 1923 report lists Chilcotin, B.C. Training Area land acquired from British Columbia; BC Geographical Names confirms the official training-area identity and later naming history; CanadaBuys/DND material documents current DND ownership/use as a military training area. Use 1923 as acquisition/use floor, not a construction date.

overrides.name: Champ de manoeuvre Sussex
overrides.source_notes: GeoNB lists Champ de manoeuvre Sussex as a Canadian Forces Range and/or Training Area. MilitaryBruce states Camp Sussex opened in 1885, the camp closed in 1965, the rifle range continued into the early 1980s, and part of the property/training area continued in DND/CFB Gagetown use. Confidence medium due mixed camp/range continuity.

overrides.name: Sussex Training Area
overrides.source_notes: GeoNB lists Sussex Training Area as a Canadian Forces Range and/or Training Area. MilitaryBruce states Camp Sussex opened in 1885, closed in 1965, its rifle range continued into the early 1980s, and the training area continued to be used by troops from CFB Gagetown. Confidence medium due mixed camp/range continuity.

overrides.name: Boreelkazerne
overrides.source_notes: Deventer planning/history sources state the Boreelkazerne was built in 1849 and that the site remained military terrain until 1997, when the last military users left and the municipality took control.

overrides.name: Generaal Majoor de Ruyter van Steveninck Kazerne
overrides.source_notes: Dutch Defence identifies the kazerne as the current home of the regiment; regimental material documents original 1946 buildings at the Oirschot kazerne. Use 1946 as a conservative facility start floor.

overrides.name: Koning Willem III Kazerne
overrides.source_notes: Apeldoorn history page states the Koning Willem III Kazerne was officially taken into use on 10 May 1939. Rijksvastgoedbedrijf confirms current continuing military real-estate use through recent building work.

overrides.name: Oranje-Nassau Kazerne
overrides.source_notes: Official site timeline states the kazerne was completed in 1813 and taken into use by King Willem I in 1814; it was transferred to Amsterdam in 1989 and converted to housing/offices.

overrides.name: Mainfranken-Kaserne
overrides.source_notes: Local and site brochure sources state the Mainfranken-Kaserne was newly built/opened in 1986 and remains a Bundeswehr location.

overrides.name: Saaleck-Kaserne
overrides.source_notes: Engineering project page for the Hammelburg Bundeswehr site states the Saaleck-Kaserne has been used militarily since 1895 and documents current Bundeswehr development work.

overrides.name: Lager Schwarzenborn

operational_intervals.label: Wehrmacht training-area and camp phase
Bundeswehr training-area and camp phase

overrides.source_notes: Hessian historical gazetteer states Lager Schwarzenborn has existed as a military training area since 1936, was a lung sanatorium in 1948-1959, then again a military training area; local history states the Bundeswehr took over/use resumed in 1956.

overrides.name: Oberfeld
overrides.source_notes: Austrian Ministry of Defence article says the Dachstein/Oberfeld training area was founded in 1930 and military use ended in 2009.

overrides.name: Maria Theresien Kaserne
overrides.source_notes: Denkmal-Heer gives military barracks naming/use from 1940; Austrian Defence current Standort page lists units at Maria Theresien-Kaserne.

overrides.name: LLanos de Armilla
overrides.source_notes: Official Spanish Air and Space Force centenary history says Aeródromo de los Llanos de Armilla was officially inaugurated on 20 June 1922 and remains Base Aérea de Armilla.

overrides.name: Cuartel General del Ejercito del Aire
overrides.source_notes: Public architectural history says the headquarters was already fulfilling its mission in 1954; Spanish Defence heritage page confirms the current headquarters/archive location.

overrides.name: Kaartinkasarmi
overrides.source_notes: Senate Properties says Kaartin kasarmi was built for the Finnish training battalion; Finnish Architecture Navigator gives the officers building completion as 1822 and later Ministry of Defence use.

overrides.name: Elias Beeckmankazerne
overrides.source_notes: Atlas van Ede says Elias Beeckmankazerne opened in 1939; Bezoek Ede says military presence at the Ede barracks ended at the end of 2010.

overrides.name: Setermoen leir
overrides.source_notes: Forsvarsbygg lists Setermoen I/II as established in 1897 with current function as training garrison; Store norske leksikon corroborates early establishment and current defence role.

overrides.name: 8th Shekari Air Base
overrides.source_notes: Khatami/8th TFB at Isfahan is tied to Iran's F-14 infrastructure; first Tomcats reached 8th TFB on 1976-01-26. Use as operational evidence, not construction proof.

overrides.name: Al Qusayr Air Base
overrides.source_notes: GlobalSecurity has dated imagery for 1987-04-22 and later ORBAT listing. This is earliest observed evidence, not construction proof.

overrides.name: An Nasiriyah Airbase
overrides.source_notes: GlobalSecurity dated imagery supports existence by 1987-04-22; no safe construction/end date found.

overrides.name: Khalkhalah Air Base
overrides.source_notes: GlobalSecurity dated imagery supports existence by 1987-04-22; no safe construction/end date found.

overrides.name: Marj Ruhayyil
overrides.source_notes: GlobalSecurity dated imagery supports existence by 1987-04-22; no safe construction/end date found.

overrides.name: Sayqal
overrides.source_notes: GlobalSecurity dated imagery supports existence by 1989-08-22; no safe construction/end date found.

overrides.name: Matan al-Sarra Air Base
overrides.source_notes: Credibly documented as a major Libyan air/ground base attacked on 1987-09-05. Use 1987 as observed operational evidence, not construction date.

overrides.name: Sweihan Airbase
overrides.source_notes: Public source says the facility was built around 1988-1990 and upgraded 2010-2014; 1990 is the conservative end of the build range.

overrides.name: Sakhir Airbase
overrides.source_notes: Construction began circa 2006; formal opening was January 2010. Treat as royal-flight/new airfield facility, not a combat base with known based units.

overrides.name: Gukbanggwahakyeonguso
overrides.source_notes: Matches ADD/Defense Science Research Institute at Daejeon; official ADD history has the Daejeon R&D Center established on 1974-02-16. Use 1974 for the mapped facility.

overrides.name: Yukgun-hanggonghakgyo
overrides.source_notes: Army Aviation School institution was created 1957-07-01, but source says it moved to the current Nonsan base in 1995; use 1995 for the coordinate-specific facility.

overrides.name: Meiktila Air Base
overrides.source_notes: Public history identifies the site as formerly RAF Meiktila, built/used from 1942, and now Myanmar Air Force Meiktila Air Base.

overrides.name: Nampong Air Base
overrides.source_notes: Evidence ties current Nampong/West Nampong to WWII Namponmao Airfield, used by USAAF 4th Combat Cargo Group from June 1945; continuity to current military use is plausible but not richly documented.

overrides.name: Sheikh Hasina cantonment
overrides.source_notes: Public reporting says the newly set-up cantonment was inaugurated on 2018-02-08; no facility closure date found.
